inconsistencies: #36114 and #35358 address the same problem (external signers returning tampered outputs or unsafe sighash types). They should be reviewed as one decision; #36114 first, since it also merges rather than replaces the returned PSBT and rebuilds the mock signer, with #35358 treated as the alternative/subset.

#36330 and #34533 are competing fixes for the same private-broadcast rebroadcast leak (skip resubmission entirely vs. route resubmission through private broadcast). Only one can land; the approach decision should be taken before either is reviewed in depth. Review #36330 first as the simpler behaviour and because it also covers mempool insertion at wallet load.

Dependency chain: #32895 (version records) and #33033 (SQLite statement RAII) are prerequisites for #33034 (transactions table), which in turn unblocks #27865 (no-longer-spendable TXO tracking). #27865 is listed above them for value, but review order must be 32895/33033 -> 33034 -> 27865.

#36070, #35918 and #36143 are three separate building blocks for the same multisig setup wizard project (#35645), each adding key/descriptor construction or parsing API surface. They should be looked at as a set so the APIs do not overlap or diverge.

#32966 (Silent Payments receiving) and #35302 (Silent Payments sending) are two halves of one project; sending additionally depends on #35301, which is not in this list. Receiving should be reviewed first.

#35989, #36342 and #36339 are the same class of bug (signed-integer overflow on extreme wallet RPC arguments causing an abort or bad funding). They now share a band and are adjacent; reviewing them together would keep the bounds-checking approach consistent.

#35317 fixes the ignored snake_case subtract_fee_from_outputs option, while #35433 deprecates a different wallet RPC argument. Reviewers on #35317 prefer a project-wide naming transition over one-off aliases; the underlying RPC-argument-naming decision should be settled before either alias/deprecation approach is merged.

#34520 (blanket [[nodiscard]] hygiene) overlaps in technique with #35998 (nodiscard on WalletBatch); only #35998 carries the fund-safety motivation, and #34520 should not be taken as covering the same ground.
#35224 states it waits on #34861, which is not in this category list; its band assumes the underlying importdescriptors error-reporting problem, not the dependency.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly along the rubric's own ordering: a small P1 set of silent balance-correctness and load-crash bugs, a large P2 block of wallet-corruption/backup/migration hardening plus the two big privacy features and the storage-refactor chain, then a long P3 tail of narrower bug fixes, RPC ergonomics, refactors and test coverage. Four bands were adjusted for consistency: #36245 up to P1, #36339 down to P2, #33033 up to P2 (chain prerequisite), #30343 up to P3 (parity with the other maintainability cleanups). Many P3 position shifts come from regrouping the band into bug fixes, then features, then cleanups, then test-only work, rather than from any change in judged importance.
